items.title: Google Public Sector and SUNY launch AI-enabled platform to accelerate university research
items.author: Matt SchneiderManaging Director, U.S. Education, State and Local GovernmentGoogle Public Sector
items.content:
Public research universities solve some of society’s most urgent challenges, but turning ideas into breakthroughs requires fast, secure access to cutting edge technology. In the agentic AI era institutions have an unprecedented opportunity to harness intelligent systems that can process massive datasets, run complex workflows, and dramatically accelerate the pace of scientific discovery.

Today at Gemini at Work, we’re announcing our collaboration with the State University of New York (SUNY) to launch the SUNY AI Platform, a secure AI and high-performance computing environment built on Google Cloud with Gemini Enterprise.

Initially available across nine of SUNY’s most research-intensive campuses, the platform is designed to help researchers move from hypothesis to discovery faster—and to help prepare New York’s students and workforce for an AI-driven economy.

Research with real-world impact

SUNY researchers are tackling challenges with direct impact for communities across New York and beyond. Their work includes improving weather prediction, detecting water quality issues, sequencing DNA for cancer treatments, and processing high-resolution brain scans to aid diagnosis.

To support that work, the SUNY AI Platform empowers researchers of all technical backgrounds to easily access and benefit from Google Cloud's advanced capabilities—bringing storage, high-powered computing, Gemini Enterprise, and more than 200 trusted AI models together into a seamless, centralized ecosystem. Rather than requiring individual teams and campuses to assemble these capabilities independently, researchers can work within a common foundation that helps simplify data analysis, enable collaboration across institutions, and apply consistent governance and responsible AI practices.

Equipping the SUNY community with AI-ready skills

Technology alone does not create impact; people do.

As part of this collaboration, SUNY is offering system-wide access to Google’s self-paced, industry-recognized AI credentials, available at no cost to students and faculty. Each course can be completed in 5-10 hours and requires no prior experience, helping learners build practical skills to write effective prompts, solve complex problems, and use AI tools responsibly. SUNY is also working to embed Google Career Certificates into academic programs so students can graduate with job-ready technical capabilities alongside their degrees.

Together, the SUNY AI Platform and these learning opportunities reflect a broader approach to AI adoption: pairing access to advanced technology with the skills and institutional capacity needed to put it to work responsibly.

To explore SUNY’s free AI learning tools and resources, visit suny.edu/google. Then read our case study here and watch our featured partnership video with Catherine Stollar Peters, SUNY’s Director of Research Data Strategy, to hear how academic leaders are using AI to transform education and the public sector.

You can also join us at the Google Public Sector Summit on October 20 to hear firsthand how leaders are using AI to transform organizations across the public sector.

items.title: Where mission meets moonshot: Join us at the Google Public Sector Summit 2026
items.author: Katharyn WhiteDirector of Marketing, Public SectorGoogle Cloud
items.content:
Across the public sector, the question has shifted from “what’s possible?” to “how can we drive mission impact?” We’ll be answering this question at the Google Public Sector Summit on October 20th at the Ronald Reagan Building in Washington, D.C.

This year’s summit brings together public sector leaders, creators, and builders to architect what’s next and bridge the gap between ambitious innovation and secure, scaled execution. Together, we’ll explore how public sector organizations are harnessing Google’s secure, integrated AI stack—encompassing everything from planet-scale infrastructure to leading models and agentic platforms—to turn ambitious moonshot aspirations into real-world outcomes that drive mission impact.

The Google Public Sector Summit is a celebration of what’s possible when human ambition and powerful technology come together in support of mission. Keep reading for a preview of the event, and how to make the most of your onsite experience.

Opening Keynote: Where Mission Meets Moonshot

Get inspired during our opening keynote which will feature , CEO of Google Public Sector,, CEO of Google Cloud, and , Field CTO of Google Public Sector. They will share real-world customer examples and live product demonstrations that showcase Google’s technology in action across the public sector. Attendees will also get the opportunity to hear from public sector leaders who are collaborating with Google and applying technology to transform missions and power moonshots.

General Session: Cloud Talks

Join , Managing Director of Customer Engineering for Google Public Sector, as she hosts a series of talks that dive deeper into the critical pillars of public sector transformation including infrastructure, AI, and security. Hear from VP of Engineering for Google Cloud, , VP of Product Management for Gemini, and , VP of Google Threat Intelligence, as they share strategies for establishing an infrastructure foundation for the agentic era, building safely with Google’s platforms, and implementing proactive defense at planet scale.

Breakouts: Panel Discussions and Birds of a Feather

Hear from Google Public Sector executives, industry partners, and leaders across defense, federal civilian, higher education, and state and local government through a series of panels and birds of a feather discussions.

  • From fragmented to fluid: Connecting data to build the agentic future. Moderated by Managing Director of Partner and Specialty Sales, this session will explore how agencies can break down legacy data silos and build a unified, AI-ready data foundation. Speakers include , CDAO Principal Deputy Chief Digital and AI Officer, , NOAA Administrator and Undersecretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere, and , Accenture Global Lead for the Google Business Group. An additional speaker, , DLA CIO, has been invited.
  • Automating defense: Securing the agentic era against complex threats. Moderated by , Managing Director and Chief Security Officer, panelists will discuss how they’re applying autonomous AI and threat intelligence to protect dynamic environments at machine speed. Speakers include , U.S. Navy CTO, , DOE-NNSA CIO, Vice Admiral (Ret.) , Texas Cyber Command Chief, and , Rhombus Power Senior Vice President of Strategic Capabilities.
  • The agentic era: Advancing missions and transforming the way we work. Moderated by , this session will highlight how secure, cost-efficient agentic capabilities can scale impact and advance missions. Featured speakers include , USPTO Acting Commissioner for Patents, , Case Western Reserve University CIO, and , Deloitte Managing Director, AI & Engineering and Defense, Security & Justice AI/Analytics Leader.
  • Interactive Birds of a Feather discussions. Connect directly with a small group of peers and Google experts to address critical mission blockers, share best practices, and accelerate your agency's journey beyond the pilot stage. Join discussions across a range of topics including tokenomics, migration, and compliance.

Demos, Lightning Talks and Labs

Experience Google’s innovations through hands-on labs, Lightning Talks, and demos taking place in the Mission Exchange on the showfloor. Topics will include agentic threat defense, multimodal AI citizen services, and legacy database modernization with AI.

Attendees can also join two expert-led labs:

  • Getting Started with Gemini: This introductory lab will guide participants through the fundamentals of Gemini and Gemini Notebook to summarize documents, search data and streamline daily tasks. No technical background required.
  • Build Gemini Agents: From Prompt to Prototype: This lab will help you bring your real-world agency use cases to life by building an AI agent with Gemini, with support from Google Cloud specialists.

Throughout the day, we will host Lightning Talks, which are dynamic 20-minute presentations featuring live demos and interactive Q&A that take place on the showfloor. These talks feature partner and customer speakers and showcase the "art of the practical" through live, real-world solutions.

Closing Session: What’s Your Moonshot?

Join us for an inspirational closing session that I’ll moderate with a special guest: NASA Administrator . Together, we’ll define what a moonshot means for the public sector in the agentic era and share strategies for fostering a culture of courageous problem-solving and applying technology to supercharge human ambition and ingenuity.

Register for the Google Public Sector Summit

Beyond the personalized programming and practical hands-on experiences, attendees will leave the event with a customized action plan for driving impact in their organization. Register today for the Google Public Sector Summit to gain the strategies, skills, and inspiration to turn your moonshot aspirations into a reality. Join us as we build what’s next for the public sector, together.

items.title: GKE CPU startup boost: Accelerate app starts without over-provisioning
items.author: Jakub PawełczakCloud Product Manager
items.content:
Yet, platform engineers and developers face a persistent dilemma: Applications often demand significantly more CPU power during startup than they do during steady-state operations. Sizing CPU requests for normal, steady-state usage leads to CPU throttling during launch, which can result in sluggish cold starts and readiness probe timeouts. On the flip side, over-provisioning baseline CPU requests to satisfy short-lived startup bursts wastes valuable compute resources, inflating infrastructure bills.

Today, we are excited to announce for GKE in preview. Integrated directly into GKE's Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA), CPU startup boost dynamically elevates a container's CPU allocation during initialization and seamlessly scales it back to baseline steady-state levels once the application is ready - all without restarting your containers.

Why modern applications need extra CPU at boot time

  • Python and AI/ML microservices

How CPU startup boost can help

CPU Startup Boost solves this by giving your workloads temporary vCPU "boosts" during launch, and automatically returning them to baseline once initialization completes.

  • : Reduce application initialization times by up to , accelerating auto-scaling responsiveness during unexpected traffic surges.
  • : Right-size steady-state CPU requests to fit actual runtime needs rather than paying for idle startup headroom.
  • : Dynamic resource resizing happens live inside the running container.
  • : Apply simple pod-level multiplier factors (e.g., 2x CPU during startup) or define granular, container-specific rules for complex multi-container pods.

Under the hood: Kubernetes In-place Pod Resize

without restarting the container process

DELETE FROM OrderAgentTasks WHERE OrderId = @orderId AND TaskId = @escalationTaskId AND TaskType = 'ESCALATE_UNAPPROVED_ORDER', ASSERT_ROWS_MODIFIED 1; -- COMMIT;"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f43d4fd1710>)])]>
